mainTopic: The burial of משה, imitating God's kindness, and the opening of פרק היה מביא on the סוטה's מנחה
overview: The amud finishes the story of the soldiers at בית פעור, who could not find the grave of משה no matter where they stood. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that even משה does not know where he is buried, and that he was buried near בית פעור to atone for the sin there. He explains 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו' as copying God's kindness: clothing the naked, visiting the sick, comforting mourners, and burying the dead. רבי שמלאי adds that the תורה begins and ends with גמילות חסדים. He also explains that משה longed to enter ארץ ישראל only to keep its מצוות, and God gave him the reward as if he had done them, reading a פסוק in ישעיהו phrase by phrase about משה. Then the first פרק ends, and the new פרק, היה מביא, opens with a משנה about the plain barley מנחה of the סוטה. The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying she is tired out so that she will confess. It then asks whether the real reason might be to keep the מגילה from being erased, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The soldiers cannot find the grave of משה
steps.stepSummary: The soldiers at בית פעור try to find the grave of משה. Wherever they stand, the grave seems to be somewhere else. This fulfills the פסוק that no man knows his grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: The government told the garrison at בית פעור: 'Show us where משה is buried.' When they stood on top of the mountain, the grave looked like it was below. When they stood below, it looked like it was above. So they split into two groups. Those on top saw it below, and those below saw it above. This fulfilled the פסוק: 'And no man knows of his grave.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began on the previous daf. Soldiers search for the grave of משה and fail in a miraculous way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting into two groups should have solved the problem, since each group could check the other's spot. But the illusion followed both groups at once. So the hiddenness of the grave is not just a lack of information; it is a miracle that keeps the פסוק true.

keyTerms.meaning: A garrison, a group of soldiers stationed in one place
The place near where משה was buried

phrases.english: the garrison of Beth Peor:
phrases.notes: This sentence starts on the previous daf: the government sent a message to the soldiers stationed at בית פעור.

phrases.english: Show us where Moses is buried.
They stood above — it appeared to them to be below,
below — it appeared to them to be above.
They divided into two groups,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָן שֶׁעוֹמְדִים לְמַעְלָה — נִדְמָה לָהֶן לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: to those standing above — it appeared to be below,
to those below — it appeared to be above,
to fulfill that which is stated:
“And no man knows of his grave.”
phrases.notes: דברים 34:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a story begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grave of משה is miraculously hidden, fulfilling 'ולא ידע איש את קבורתו'.

steps.title: Even משה himself does not know where he is buried
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא goes further: not even משה knows the location of his own grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: Even משה רבינו does not know where he is buried.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא makes a bold claim about the same פסוק. The hiddenness applies even to משה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story showed that other people cannot find the grave. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא extends this to משה. The next step will show where in the פסוק he sees this.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא; author of the statements in this section

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ הֵיכָן קָבוּר.
phrases.english: Even Moses our teacher does not know where he is buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ הֵיכָן קָבוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same פסוק and widens its scope to include משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה himself does not know where he is buried.

steps.title: The word 'man' links the two verses
steps.stepSummary: The source is a word-link: 'איש' in 'no man knows his grave' and 'משה איש האלהים'. Since משה is called 'איש', he is included in 'no man'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'And no man knows of his grave,' and it is written there: 'And this is the blessing with which משה, the man of God, blessed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof for רבי חמא's claim. It compares the word 'man' in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says no 'איש' knows the grave. Elsewhere the תורה calls משה an 'איש'. So the 'איש' who does not know includes משה himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The man of God, a title of משה

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וְלֹא יָדַע אִישׁ אֶת קְבֻרָתוֹ״,
phrases.english: It is written here: “And no man knows of his grave,”
and it is written there:
“And this is the blessing wherewith blessed
Moses the man of God.”
phrases.notes: דברים 33:1. Since משה is called 'איש' here, 'no איש knows' includes him too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That משה does not know his own burial place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word 'איש' in דברים 34:6 and דברים 33:1.

steps.title: משה was buried near בית פעור to bring atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains why משה was buried near בית פעור: to atone for the sin of פעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: Why was משה buried near בית פעור? To atone for what happened at פעור.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement of the same אמורא asks why משה was buried in that spot. The answer is to atone for the sin there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burial place has a purpose: the sin of פעור needed atonement, and the grave of the righteous משה nearby provides it. The question is asked and answered in one breath, so it is a single statement, not a back-and-forth argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The incident of פעור, the sin of Israel there

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה נִקְבַּר מֹשֶׁה אֵצֶל בֵּית פְּעוֹר —
phrases.english: For what reason was Moses buried near Beth Peor?
In order to atone for the incident of Peor.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה נִקְבַּר מֹשֶׁה אֵצֶל בֵּית פְּעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching by the same אמורא about the burial of משה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה was buried near בית פעור to atone for the sin of פעור.

steps.title: What does 'walk after ה׳' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא asks for the meaning of the פסוק 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: What is the meaning of the פסוק: 'After ה׳ your God you shall walk'?
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. It quotes a פסוק and asks what it really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מאי דכתיב' signals that the plain meaning of the פסוק is puzzling. The next step will explain what the problem is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
“After the Lord your God shall you walk”?
phrases.notes: דברים 13:5

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב אַחֲרֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם תֵּלֵכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third teaching by the same אמורא, on a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true meaning of the command to walk after ה׳.

steps.title: A person cannot literally follow God
steps.stepSummary: The literal reading is impossible. One cannot walk after the שכינה, since God is called a consuming fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really possible for a person to walk after the שכינה? Doesn't a פסוק already say: 'For ה׳ your God is a consuming fire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the פסוק cannot mean walking after God physically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another פסוק describes God as 'אש אוכלה', a consuming fire, and no one can come close to fire. So the literal reading clashes with a different פסוק, and a new explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: But hasn't it already been stated

phrases.english: But is it possible for a person
to walk after the Divine Presence?
But hasn't it already been stated:
“For the Lord your God is a devouring fire”!
phrases.notes: דברים 4:24

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְאָדָם לְהַלֵּךְ אַחַר שְׁכִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in step 5 is a real problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: God is a consuming fire, so physically following Him is impossible.

steps.title: Follow God's ways, not God's location
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'walking after ה׳' means copying the מדות of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means to follow the ways and qualities of הקדוש ברוך הוא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of the פסוק. It also sets up a list of examples that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אחרי' is moved from a physical meaning to a moral one. We follow God by acting the way He acts. The examples that follow show what this looks like in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: His qualities, His ways of acting
The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the מצוה of imitating God through acts of kindness (גמילות חסדים).

phrases.english: Rather, to walk after the attributes
of the Holy One, Blessed be He:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְהַלֵּךְ אַחַר מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might seem to mean physically following God.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means imitating God's ways of acting.

steps.title: Clothing the naked
steps.stepSummary: God clothed אדם and חוה, so we too must clothe the naked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as He clothes the naked, as it says: 'And ה׳ God made for אדם and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them' — so too you should clothe the naked.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first example of copying God's ways, with a פסוק showing God did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example follows a pattern: a kind act of God, a פסוק proving He did it, and then 'אף אתה', meaning you do the same. Here the act is giving clothing.

phrases.english: Just as He clothes the naked,
as it is written: “And the Lord God made
for Adam and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them” —
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:21

phrases.english: so too, you should clothe the naked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First example of the principle in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That God clothes the naked, so we must too.

steps.title: Visiting the sick
steps.stepSummary: God visited אברהם when he was recovering, so we too must visit the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא visited the sick, as it says: 'And ה׳ appeared to him in the plains of ממרא' — so too you should visit the sick.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second example: visiting the sick, learned from God appearing to אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God appeared to אברהם while he was healing after his ברית מילה. The גמרא reads this appearance as a visit to a sick person.

keyTerms.meaning: The plains or trees of ממרא, where אברהם lived

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, visited the sick,
as it is written: “And the Lord appeared unto him by the terebinths of Mamre” —
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:1. This comes right after אברהם's ברית מילה, while he was recovering.

phrases.english: so too, you should visit the sick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second example of the principle in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That God visits the sick, so we must too.

steps.title: Comforting mourners
steps.stepSummary: God blessed יצחק after אברהם died, which was comforting a mourner. So we too must comfort mourners.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא comforted mourners, as it says: 'And it was after the death of אברהם that God blessed יצחק his son' — so too you should comfort mourners.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third example: comforting mourners, learned from God blessing יצחק after his father's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing in the פסוק is the key. God's blessing came 'after the death of אברהם', while יצחק was mourning, so it served as comfort.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, consoled mourners,
as it is written: “And it came to pass after the death of Abraham,
that God blessed Isaac his son” —
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:11

phrases.english: so too, you should console mourners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third example of the principle in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That God comforts mourners, so we must too.

steps.title: Burying the dead
steps.stepSummary: God buried משה, so we too must bury the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא buried the dead, as it says: 'And He buried him in the valley' — so too you should bury the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth example: burying the dead, learned from God burying משה. It brings the section back to where it began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof פסוק is the same one about the burial of משה from the start of the section. The burier in 'ויקבר אותו בגי' is understood as God Himself, so the burial of משה becomes the model for our מצוה of burying the dead.
steps.whatToRemember: 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו' means copying God's kindness: clothing the naked, visiting the sick, comforting mourners, and burying the dead.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, buried the dead,
as it is written: “And He buried him in the valley” —
phrases.notes: דברים 34:6. This is about משה, the same פסוק as 'no man knows of his grave.'

phrases.english: so too, you should bury the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth example of the principle in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That God buries the dead, so we must too.

steps.title: What were the garments of skin?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about what the כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר that God made for אדם and חוה were.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Garments of skin.' רב and שמואל disagree. One says it was something that comes from skin. The other says it was something that the skin enjoys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק about God clothing אדם and חוה from step 8 and asks what the 'garments of skin' were. רב and שמואל give two explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'skin' can be read two ways. One opinion reads it as the material: clothing made from an animal's skin. The other reads it as the person's own skin: clothing that feels good on the body.

keyTerms.meaning: One says (used when two אמוראים disagree and we don't say which said what)

phrases.english: "Garments of skin."
phrases.notes: These are the words from the פסוק in step 8 about God clothing אדם and חוה.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: דָּבָר הַבָּא מִן הָעוֹר,
phrases.english: One says: something that comes from the skin,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: דָּבָר שֶׁהָעוֹר נֶהֱנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: and one says: something that the skin benefits from.
phrases.notes: Here 'skin' means the person's own skin, so it was clothing that felt good on the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side point explaining a word in the פסוק used as a proof in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The garments were either made from skin, or made for the skin's comfort.

steps.title: The תורה begins and ends with kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי teaches that the תורה starts with God clothing אדם and חוה and ends with God burying משה. Both are acts of גמילות חסדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי taught: The תורה begins with kindness and ends with kindness. It begins with kindness, as it says: 'ה׳ God made garments of skin for אדם and his wife and clothed them.' It ends with kindness, as it says: 'And He buried him in the valley.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי makes a new point: kindness frames the whole תורה, from beginning to end. He brings one פסוק from the start of the תורה and one from the very end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same two examples from steps 8 and 11 (clothing and burying) are now used for a new idea. Before, they showed which מדות we must copy. Here they show that the whole תורה is wrapped in חסד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that kindness is not just one מצוה among many. It is the frame that the whole תורה sits in.

phrases.english: Rabbi Samlai taught:
The Torah: its beginning is acts of kindness,
and its end is acts of kindness.
Its beginning is acts of kindness:
as it is written: "And ה׳ God made for Adam and for his wife
garments of skin, and clothed them,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:21

phrases.english: and its end is acts of kindness:
as it is written: "And He buried him in the valley."
phrases.notes: דברים 34:6. This is about God burying משה, right at the end of the תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי: תּוֹרָה תְּחִלָּתָהּ גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching that reuses the clothing and burial פסוקים from steps 8 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah opens and closes with God doing kindness.

steps.title: Why did משה want to enter ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי asks why משה wanted so badly to enter ארץ ישראל. Surely it was not for the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי taught: Why did משה רבינו long to enter ארץ ישראל? Did he need to eat its fruit? Or did he need to fill up on its good things?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי opens a new teaching with a question. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question pushes away the simple reason, enjoying the land's food, as something that could not be true of משה. That leaves room for a deeper reason, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really that...? (asks a question that expects 'no')

phrases.english: Rabbi Samlai taught:
For what reason did Moshe our teacher long
to enter Eretz Yisrael?
Did he need to eat from its fruit?!
Or did he need to be satisfied from its goodness?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה נִתְאַוָּה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לִיכָּנֵס לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate teaching of רבי שמלאי, connected to the theme of משה from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the real reason משה wanted to enter the land?

steps.title: משה wanted to keep the מצוות of the land
steps.stepSummary: משה wanted to enter so that he could keep the many מצוות that can only be done in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what משה said: Israel was given many מצוות that can only be kept in ארץ ישראל. Let me enter the land so that I can keep all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question from step 14. משה's longing was for מצוות, not for food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some מצוות, like those tied to the land and its crops, only apply in ארץ ישראל. משה wanted to have a chance to keep every מצוה, so he needed to be in the land.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what Moshe said:
Israel was commanded many מצוות,
and they can only be fulfilled in Eretz Yisrael.
phrases.notes: He means some of the מצוות, the ones that only apply in the land.

phrases.english: Let me enter the land
so that all of them will be fulfilled through me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה wanted to keep the מצוות that only apply in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: God gives משה the reward as if he did them
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells משה that he will get the reward as if he had kept those מצוות. This is supported by a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to him: Are you looking for anything except to get the reward? I will count it for you as if you did them. As it says: 'Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will share spoils with the mighty, because he poured out his soul to death, and was counted with the sinners, and he carried the sin of many, and prayed for the sinners.'
steps.whatsHappening: God answers משה's wish. Even though משה will not enter the land, he gets full credit for those מצוות, and a פסוק is brought to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal of doing the מצוות is to earn their reward. Since משה truly wanted to do them, God counts it as if he did. The פסוק describes someone who gets a great portion because he gave himself up for the people, and the גמרא reads it as being about משה.

keyTerms.meaning: I will count it for you

steps.whatToRemember: משה longed for ארץ ישראל only to keep its מצוות. God counted it as if he had kept them. A real desire to do a מצוה can bring its reward even when it cannot be done.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ אֶלָּא לְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר?
phrases.english: Are you asking for anything other than to receive reward?
I will count it for you as if you did them,
as it is said: "Therefore I will give him a portion among the great,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 53:12

phrases.english: and with the mighty he will divide spoil,
because he poured out his soul to death,
and was counted with the sinners,
and he carried the sin of many,
and pleaded for the sinners."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: כְּלוּם אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ אֶלָּא לְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God's response to משה's reason given in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That משה receives reward as if he kept the מצוות of the land
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: משה gets full reward for the מצוות of ארץ ישראל, as if he had done them.

steps.title: משה's reward is like that of the אבות
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says משה will get a share 'among the great.' That could mean the later great people, so the next words, 'with the mighty,' show it means אברהם, יצחק and יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Therefore I will give him a share among the great.' You might think this means like the later great people and not like the earlier ones. So the פסוק adds: 'And with the mighty he will divide the spoil.' This means like אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, who were mighty in תורה and מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining, one phrase at a time, the פסוק from ישעיהו that was used in Step 16. The first phrase tells us how big משה's reward is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Among the great' alone could mean any great people, even later ones who are on a lower level. The second half of the פסוק, 'with the mighty,' sets the level: משה's reward is equal to the אבות, who were 'mighty' in תורה and מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think...' It brings up a possible wrong reading of the פסוק.
'The פסוק teaches us.' It brings in the words that block the wrong reading.
Mighty ones. Here it means people who are great in תורה and מצוות.
The earlier generations and the later generations.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is still explaining the same ישעיהו פסוק from Step 16. It is now going through it piece by piece.

phrases.english: "Therefore I will give him a share among the great."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 53:12. This is the same פסוק from Step 16, and here 'him' means משה.

phrases.english: You might think: like the later ones and not like the earlier ones,
so the פסוק teaches: "And with the mighty he will divide the spoil,"
meaning like אברהם, יצחק and יעקב,
who are mighty in תורה and in מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל כָּאַחֲרוֹנִים וְלֹא כָּרִאשׁוֹנִים, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in detail the פסוק that Step 16 used as its support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's reward is on the level of the אבות.

steps.title: משה was ready to give up his life for כלל ישראל
steps.stepSummary: 'He poured out his soul to death' means משה offered to die for the people, as he said, 'Erase me from Your book.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Because he poured out his soul to death': this means he gave himself over to death, as it says, 'And if not, please erase me...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next phrase of the פסוק. It is the reason משה gets this reward: he was ready to die for the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'poured out his soul to death' is tied to what משה said after the חטא העגל. He asked to be erased from ה׳'s book if the people were not forgiven. That shows he was ready to give up everything for כלל ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Poured out or laid bare. It means he gave up his life completely.
He gave himself over to death.

phrases.english: "Because he poured out his soul to death,"
meaning that he gave himself over to death,
as it says: "And if not, please erase me, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:32. The 'etc.' means the rest of the פסוק: 'from Your book that You have written.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the same ישעיהו פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה offered his own life for the people.

steps.title: משה was counted with those who died in the מדבר
steps.stepSummary: 'He was counted with sinners' means משה was counted with the generation that died in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he was counted with sinners': this means he was counted with those who died in the מדבר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next phrase. משה ended up in the same group as the people who died in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to Steps 14-16. משה did not enter ארץ ישראל, just like the generation of the מדבר. The פסוק calls that group 'sinners.'

keyTerms.meaning: The people who died in the מדבר.

phrases.english: "And he was counted with sinners" —
meaning that he was counted with those who died in the מדבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה shared the fate of the generation of the מדבר.

steps.title: משה gained forgiveness for the חטא העגל
steps.stepSummary: 'He carried the sin of many' means משה gained forgiveness for the חטא העגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he carried the sin of many': this means he gained forgiveness for the incident of the עגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next phrase. It is about משה getting forgiveness for the people after the עגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Carrying the sin of many' is read as משה taking on the job of getting forgiveness for the whole nation. The 'many' here is all of כלל ישראל, who sinned with the עגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The incident of the golden calf.

phrases.english: "And he carried the sin of many" —
meaning that he gained forgiveness for the incident of the עגל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה brought forgiveness for the חטא העגל.

steps.title: משה davened that sinners should do תשובה
steps.stepSummary: 'He would plead for the sinners' means משה asked for רחמים that the sinners of ישראל should do תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he would plead for the sinners': this means he asked for mercy for the sinners of ישראל, that they should come back in תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last phrase of the פסוק. It reads the word יפגיע as davening for the sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 was about forgiveness for a sin that already happened. This phrase is about the sinners themselves: משה davened that they should change and do תשובה. The next step will prove that the word פגיעה really means תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked for mercy, meaning he davened.
Coming back to ה׳, which is repentance.

phrases.english: "And he would plead for the sinners" —
meaning that he asked for mercy for the sinners of ישראל
that they should come back in תשובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה davened for the sinners to do תשובה.

steps.title: Proof that פגיעה means תפלה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ירמיהו puts 'do not pray' next to 'do not plead (תפגע) with Me,' which shows that פגיעה means תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And פגיעה means nothing other than תפלה, as it says: 'And you, do not daven for this people, and do not raise for them a cry or a prayer, and do not plead with Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for how it read the word יפגיע in Step 21. It shows from another פסוק that this word means davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו‎, ה׳ tells the נביא not to daven for the people. In that same line, 'do not plead (תפגע)' sits right next to the words for prayer. So we see that פגיעה is a kind of תפלה, and Step 21's reading is backed up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'X means nothing other than Y.' It is a way of defining a word.
Pleading or interceding. Here it is shown to mean תפלה.
A cry, meaning a loud prayer.

steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק in ישעיהו is read about משה: his reward is like the אבות, he was ready to die for the people, he died in the מדבר, he gained forgiveness for the עגל, and he davened for sinners to do תשובה.

phrases.english: And פגיעה means nothing other than prayer,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעַד הָעָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: as it says: "And you, do not pray for this people,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 7:16.

phrases.english: and do not raise for them a cry or a prayer,
and do not plead with Me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the meaning of יפגיע used in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That the word פגיעה (יפגיע) means תפלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 7:16, where תפגע appears next to תתפלל and תפלה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המקנא לאשתו
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of סוטה, המקנא לאשתו, ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, המקנא לאשתו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the פרק. It is not part of the discussion itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said when finishing a פרק. It shows our love for the learning and our wish to come back to it. The name of the פרק comes from its first words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you.' It is said when finishing a פרק.
'One who warns his wife.' This is the name of the first פרק of סוטה.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "המקנא לאשתו"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק after the aggadah about משה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of סוטה is finished.

steps.title: The סוטה holds her מנחה in a plain basket to tire her out
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק begins: the husband brings the סוטה's מנחה in a plain Egyptian basket and puts it in her hands so that she gets tired.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would bring her מנחה in a plain Egyptian basket, and put it in her hands, in order to tire her out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה and a new פרק (היה מביא) begin. It describes how the סוטה's מנחה is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike other מנחות, this one is first carried in a cheap basket, not a כלי שרת. It is put in the woman's hands so that she becomes tired during the process. Being worn out might lead her to admit the truth instead of drinking the water.

keyTerms.meaning: Her מנחה, a flour offering brought for the סוטה.
An Egyptian basket, a plain basket woven from palm branches.

phrases.english: He would bring her מנחה
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband. These first words, היה מביא, are also the name of the new פרק.

phrases.english: inside an Egyptian basket
and he puts it in her hands
in order to tire her out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's מנחה is brought in a plain basket and placed in her hands to tire her.

steps.title: Her offering starts in a basket, not a holy vessel
steps.stepSummary: Every other מנחה is in a כלי שרת from start to finish, but the סוטה's מנחה starts in a plain Egyptian basket and only ends in a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: All meal-offerings are in a holy service vessel from beginning to end. This one starts in an Egyptian basket and only ends up in a service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from step 24 and gives the first way the סוטה's מנחה is different from every other מנחה: what it is carried in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a מנחה is in a כלי שרת for the whole process. Here the first stage happens in a cheap, plain basket, the same basket from step 24. Only later is it moved into a כלי שרת so it can be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal-offerings, which are קרבנות made of flour
A holy vessel used for the עבודה in the בית המקדש
A plain Egyptian basket made of palm leaves

phrases.english: All meal-offerings, their beginning and their end
are in a service vessel,
but this one, its beginning is in an Egyptian basket,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the סוטה's מנחה. It is the same basket the husband carried in step 24.

phrases.english: and its end is in a service vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת תְּחִילָּתָן וְסוֹפָן בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the סוטה's מנחה by contrasting it with other מנחות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's מנחה begins in a plain basket and only ends in a כלי שרת, unlike every other מנחה.

steps.title: No oil and no frankincense
steps.stepSummary: Other מנחות need oil and frankincense, but the סוטה's מנחה needs neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: All meal-offerings need oil and frankincense. This one needs neither oil nor frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second difference: the סוטה's מנחה is missing the oil and frankincense that a regular מנחה has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil and frankincense make a מנחה rich and fragrant. Leaving them out makes this offering plain and bare. The משנה here states the rule but does not give a reason for it.

phrases.english: All meal-offerings require oil and frankincense,
but this one does not require
either oil or frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second contrast in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's מנחה has no oil and no frankincense.

steps.title: Barley flour, and how it differs from the עומר
steps.stepSummary: Other מנחות come from wheat, but this one comes from barley. The מנחת העומר is also barley, but it is fine groats, while the סוטה's is plain flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: All meal-offerings come from wheat, and this one comes from barley. The עומר offering also comes from barley, but it was brought as fine groats, and this one is brought as plain flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third difference, that it is made of barley. Then it heads off an objection from the מנחת העומר, which is also barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the barley point fails, because the עומר is barley too. The משנה answers that the עומר is high-quality sifted groats, while the סוטה's מנחה is coarse, plain flour. So it is still lower in quality than any other מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
Groats, fine sifted grain of high quality
Plain flour that has not been sifted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the עומר disproves the barley point. Both are barley, but the עומר is fine quality and the סוטה's is plain flour.

phrases.english: All meal-offerings come from wheat,
but this one comes from barley.
The omer meal-offering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּאָה מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִין —
phrases.english: even though it comes from barley,
it was brought as groats,
phrases.notes: גרש means carefully sifted, top-quality grain.

phrases.english: but this one is brought as flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third contrast and handles a possible counter-example
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's מנחה is plain barley flour, lower in quality than every other מנחה, even the barley עומר.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: animal behavior, animal food
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל explains the barley: because her actions were like an animal's, her offering is animal food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: just as her actions were the actions of an animal, so her offering is animal food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives a reason for the barley rule from step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Barley was commonly fed to animals. Since she secluded herself with another man after being warned, behavior compared to an animal's, the offering matches what she did.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, the head of the סנהדרין

steps.whatToRemember: The סוטה's מנחה is made plain on purpose: a cheap basket, no oil or frankincense, and coarse barley. רבן גמליאל ties the barley to her behavior.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
just as her actions were the actions of an animal,
so her offering is animal food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּעֲשֶׂיהָ מַעֲשֵׂה בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the barley rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her offering is animal food because her behavior was like an animal's.

steps.title: Why tire her out? To get her to confess
steps.stepSummary: אבא חנין in the name of רבי אליעזר says all this effort is meant to tire her so she confesses. If the תורה cares this much about sinners, it surely cares about people who do God's will.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: אבא חנין says in the name of רבי אליעזר: Why all this? To tire her out, so she will take back her denial. If the תורה is this protective of those who go against God's will, all the more so of those who do His will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא explaining why the סוטה is made to work so hard, like holding the basket in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tiring her out pushes her to admit the truth. If she admits it, she does not drink the water and does not die. From this mercy toward a sinner, the ברייתא makes a קל וחומר: God's care for the righteous must be even greater.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
That she take back her denial and confess
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the main claim of the sugya, that the tiring comes from mercy. The next step challenges exactly this.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught: Abba Ḥanin says
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
And why all this?
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. "All this" means the tiring steps, like holding the basket from step 24.

phrases.english: In order to tire her out,
so that she will retract.
If the Torah is so protective
of those who go against His will,
all the more so of those who do His will.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא חָנִין אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by explaining the reason for the tiring in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tiring is meant to make her confess and be spared, which shows the תורה's mercy, and a קל וחומר follows for the righteous.

steps.title: Maybe the goal is to protect the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the reason is mercy. Maybe the goal is that the מגילה with God's name should not get erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know it is because the תורה is protective? Maybe it is so that the scroll will not be erased!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason in step 29 by offering a different reason for getting her to confess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she confesses, the מגילה, which has God's name written on it, never gets erased into the water. So pushing her to confess could be about honoring God's name and not about mercy for her. If that is true, the קל וחומר from step 29 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know
The סוטה's scroll, which has God's name written on it

phrases.english: And from where do we know it is because the Torah is protective?
Perhaps it is in order that
the scroll will not be erased!
phrases.notes: The פסוקים, with God's name, are written on this scroll and then erased into the water she drinks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the tiring comes from the תורה's mercy on the סוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same result, getting her to confess, could come from a different motive: protecting God's written name from being erased.

steps.title: The answer begins: רבי אליעזר holds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by explaining what רבי אליעזר holds. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to the challenge in step 30. Only the first word appears here, and the answer continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קסבר signals that the answer will rely on רבי אליעזר's own opinion about the סוטה laws. That opinion will show why the reason cannot be protecting the מגילה, so it must be mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion

phrases.english: He holds
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אליעזר. The rest of his opinion continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge about the מגילה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relies on the תנא's own position (continues beyond this section)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tiring might only be meant to keep the מגילה from being erased.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer will show from רבי אליעזר's view that the reason is mercy (finished in the next section).
